slides.title: ThreatLens
slides.subtitle: Threat modeling for SMEs in minutes
slides.notes: ThreatLens is an AI threat-modeling agent. It takes an SME's app description (free text, architecture YAML/JSON, optional OpenAPI) and produces what an AppSec consultant delivers after a 3-5 day threat-modeling engagement: asset and data-flow inventory, STRIDE threat model mapped to OWASP Top 10 2021 / ASVS 4.0.3 / CWE, risk-scored findings, a prioritised remediation plan, a Mermaid DFD and Markdown/HTML/JSON reports. Source: README.md. License MIT.

slides.title: Who we built for

items.heading: Clinics
items.body: Patient records and online booking. Health data (PHI) on the line.

items.heading: E-commerce
items.body: Stores taking payments through Paymob and Fawry callbacks.

items.heading: HR portals
items.body: Payroll, salaries and national IDs or Iqamas for Saudi staff.

slides.notes: Target users: SME founders/CTOs and 2-10 person dev teams in Egypt and Saudi Arabia without in-house security staff; freelance and agency developers building client apps; security consultants who want a first draft in seconds. Regulation increasingly expects a documented security design: Egypt PDPL 151/2020, KSA PDPL, PCI DSS, NCA ECC, SAMA (context, not legal advice). Source: README.md 'The problem' and 'Who it's for'.

slides.title: A threat model costs a week most SMEs never buy.
slides.body: 3–5 consultant days. 1–3 weeks to schedule. Stale at the next release.
slides.notes: Manual engagement length 3-5 consultant-days and 7-21 day procurement/scheduling lead time are stated assumptions in docs/impact.md (author's consulting experience, not a market survey). Consequence described in README: SMEs ship IDORs, unsigned payment callbacks and internet-exposed admin panels.

slides.title: The workflow replaced
rows: Draw the DFD and trust boundaries
STRIDE session per component and flow
Map to OWASP · ASVS · CWE and rate risk
Write the remediation roadmap and report
slides.notes: Mapping taken from README.md 'Workflow it replaces'. Manual: 3-5 days. ThreatLens: minutes including a recommended 2-4 h human review. STRIDE row = stride_analyze_component, analyze_data_flows, analyze_api_endpoints, analyze_system.

slides.title: How the agent works

items.heading: Plan
items.body: An LLM via function calling or an offline policy picks the next tool.

items.heading: Act
items.body: 12 tools share one state backed by 42 STRIDE rules and 35 mitigations.

items.heading: Reflect
items.body: A coverage self-check loops back and a guardrail completes any skipped step.

items.heading: Run anywhere
items.body: Offline with no API key or any OpenAI-compatible LLM including Ollama Cloud.

slides.notes: Source: README.md Architecture and LLM mode sections; threatlens/tools.py TOOLS registry (12 tools: parse_architecture, enumerate_components, stride_analyze_component, analyze_data_flows, analyze_api_endpoints, analyze_system, map_to_owasp, score_risk, reflect, build_remediation_plan, render_diagram, render_report). LLM providers: Ollama Cloud (OLLAMA_API_KEY alias, default gpt-oss:120b at https://ollama.com/v1), OpenAI, OpenRouter, Groq, local Ollama. In LLM mode the model drives the loop, extracts architecture from free text, adds context-specific threats (tagged LLM-proposed) and writes the executive summary. Any LLM/network error falls back to offline mode. Risk = likelihood 1-5 x impact 1-5; Critical >= 20, High >= 12, Medium >= 6.

slides.title: Demo: clinic booking
slides.notes: Example: Shifa Care Clinic Booking (Cairo/Alexandria), input examples/clinic_booking.yaml. Source: examples/output/shifa_care_clinic_booking.md executive summary and docs/impact.md. Top criticals (risk 25/25): forged Paymob webhook/callback to the Booking API (A08, CWE-345); internet-exposed admin panel without MFA (A07, CWE-308/306); IDOR on the Booking API (A01, CWE-639/862); plus payment amount tampering at 20/25 (A04). 18 'Now' actions ~28.5 dev-days; full plan 30 actions, 54 dev-days.

slides.title: Measured impact
slides.notes: Source: docs/impact.md, generated by python benchmarks/impact_benchmark.py --runs 20 (offline deterministic mode, median of 20 runs per example). Recall: 37/38 across the three benchmarked examples (clinic 14/14, e-commerce 14/14, HR 9/10; the miss was mass assignment of salary/role fields, suppressed because the API documents input validation). The checklist was written by the author before measuring and is NOT independent ground truth. Runtime: 3.8-17.9 ms median per example; LLM mode takes seconds to minutes. Time and cost figures are ESTIMATES; assumptions in docs/impact.md: manual engagement 3-5 consultant-days (24-40 h), day rate USD 500-900 (assumed, not a market survey), human review of ThreatLens output 2-4 h, offline API cost USD 0 (LLM mode adds provider token cost). Lead time: minutes vs 7-21 days (assumption). On-slide values are the conservative ends of the ranges: 83%+ = at least 83% (range 83-95%); <=$450 = USD 125-450 per model.

slides.title: Results across four SMEs
slides.notes: Sources: README.md 'Sample output' table, docs/impact.md per-example table, and the executive summaries in examples/output/*.md. Low findings: 0 in all four. All six STRIDE categories appear in each benchmarked example. Masar HR documents MFA via SSO, RBAC, audit logging, a WAF and monitoring, so ThreatLens reports fewer, lower-severity findings: documented controls suppress matching threats. Dawaa Express (Riyadh pharmacy delivery) was generated from a free-text paragraph only; it is not part of the recall benchmark. Agent time = median of 20 offline runs from docs/impact.md; Dawaa Express was not in the timing benchmark (n/a).

items.heading: Next

items.heading: Then

items.heading: Later

slides.notes: 'Shipped' reflects the repo today (README.md: v1.0.0, offline KB, OpenAI-compatible LLM mode incl. Ollama Cloud, Streamlit app, 12 offline tests). The Next/Then/Later items are PROPOSED by the author and are not committed in the repo; they are drawn from the README Limitations section (ASVS references are section-level only; the expert checklist is author-written, not independent ground truth) and from the impact claim that a model can be re-run on every architecture change. Arabic reports and regulatory evidence packs are proposals; regulatory notes are context, not legal advice.

slides.title: Run it offline today
slides.body: github.com/ahmedandaloes/threatlens — run offline in 3 commands. No API key needed.
slides.notes: Quickstart from README.md: (1) pip install -r requirements.txt (Python 3.10+); (2) python -m threatlens examples/clinic_booking.yaml; (3) open threatlens_output/shifa_care_clinic_booking.html (Linux xdg-open, Windows start). Web UI: streamlit run app.py. Docker: docker build -t threatlens . && docker run -p 8501:8501 threatlens. Ask: try it on your own architecture and review the Now actions first.
